newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index ends above 6,800 points.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index ends above 6,800 points.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks leaped to their fourth record close for the week Friday as a slew of strong earnings reports lifted the Dow Jones industrial average above 6,800 points for the first time.
The Nasdaq Composite, Standard & Poor's 500 and New York Stock Exchange indexes also finished at new highs.
The Dow ended up 67.73 points at 6,833.10, beating Thursday's record of 6,765.37. Just 12 trading sessions into the New Year, the index is up nearly 385 points, or a sizzling 6 percent.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,464 to 984 on heavy volume of 532 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said that stable interest rates and sheer momentum also propelled the markets.
"Today was a combination of factors and momentum was as much of it as anything else," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney.
"A lot of the key economic numbers are behind us which leaves earnings in control of the market," he said. "And earnings have been so far, so good."

With the earnings reporting season just a few days old, the profit reports have proven favourable and, in the meantime, the bond market has found stable footing, leaving little in the way of a stock market that continues to draw on a seasonal cash infusion and seems intent on climbing.
Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd., said, "7,000 is a foregone short-term conclusion given the behaviour of this market."
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 1/32 of a point, or 31 cents on a $1,000 bond, leaving its yield unchanged at Thursday's close of 6.83 percent.
Only a handful of companies reported their quarterly results, but among the session's standouts were several who did so late Thursday.

After the market closed, Microsoft Corp. said it earned $741 million in the latest quarter, compared with $575 million a year earlier. The per share earnings of 57 cents beat Wall Street estimates and were up from 45 cents a year earlier.
In after-hours trading, Microsoft's stock rose 1-7/8 to 89 after gaining 1-1/8 to 87-1/8 on Nasdaq.

Ascend Communications Inc. led a furious rally among networking equipment companies, surging 6-1/8 to 75. The company was upgraded by several Wall Street brokerage houses, one day after posting fourth quarter earnings that were nearly triple those of a year ago.

"The networking stocks had been subject to a lot of questions concerning their earnings and have underperformed over the last two weeks," Bleier said. "They did extremely well after Ascend's numbers."
Other stocks included Cascade Communications Corp., which rose 8-1/8 to 60, and Cisco Systems Inc., up 2-1/4 to 72-5/8.
Blue-chip stocks continued to dominate the advance, evidenced by the Dow's outperformance of other indexes like the Nasdaq Composite index.
DuPont Co. led the winners among Dow components, rising 2-7/8 to 111-5/8 after Goldman Sachs upgraded the shares.
PaineWebber Group Inc. jumped 3-5/8 to 31-3/8 on a report that the company was being eyed as a takeover target by BankAmerica Corp. and others.
After the close, however, PaineWebber issued a statement that said its chief executive had not engaged in any talks with BankAmerica. BankAmerica gained 1 to 106-7/8.
Economically-sensitive stocks performed well. Aluminum Co. of America rose 1-3/8 to 73, Caterpillar Inc. added 1 to 78-3/4 and International Paper climbed 1/2 to 43-1/8.
VLSI Technology Inc. tumbled 5-7/8 to 17-3/8. The company reported a fourth quarter loss and said its first quarter revenues would be even with or lower than the just concluded fourth quarter.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 8.47 points to a record 1,349.05.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 6.42 to 776.17, a record. The American Stock Exchange index was up 2.59 at 589.95.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 3.19 to 409.31, a record. The average share was up 33 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,501.831 up 54.184 or 0.73 percent.
